_note: FICTIONAL journey content for Stage 2 (First job). Listings, landlords, events and lease text are illustrative. Teaching points reference content.json items (each with an official source). Scam listings teach patterns only: no real names, numbers, emails or payment details. Difficulty changes wording, never the facts.

text.easy: Gorgeous 1-bed, $1,050/month! I'm overseas, so no viewings. E-transfer the first month and I'll mail the keys.
text.normal: Bright 1-bed, $1,050/month, utilities included. Owner is abroad. Keys couriered once your deposit clears.
text.hard: 1BR, $1,050/mo all-incl. Owner o/s on contract; virtual tour only. Reserve w/ deposit; keys by courier.

text.easy: Luxury condo, only $1,150/month! Book a viewing through our online form. Banking details required first.
text.normal: Condo 1-bed, $1,150/month. Our pre-approval form unlocks viewing times. Banking info required.
text.hard: 1BR condo $1,150. Pre-screening portal: ID + online banking verification req'd before showings.

text.easy: 1-bed, $1,575/month. Viewing on Saturday. Send a $200 holding fee by e-transfer first.
text.normal: 1-bed, $1,575/month. Saturday viewings. A small e-transfer holding fee secures your slot.
text.hard: 1BR $1,575. Viewings Sat. Holding fee (e-transfer) to confirm slot; non-refundable.

viewing._note: Extended only: quick questions that replace the old point-and-click viewing (PRD v3 Change 2). src/config/modes.ts sets how many a run asks.

questions.text: At a viewing, what's worth checking closely?

options.label: Stains, musty smells or rotting wood
Whether you like the paint colour
Whether the neighbours are home

feedback.right: Right: water damage is easy to miss and costly later.
feedback.wrong: Look for water damage: stains, musty smells, rotting wood.

questions.text: There's no smoke alarm. Whose job is it to install one?

options.label: The landlord's
Yours, once you move in
Nobody's, it's optional

feedback.right: Right: in Toronto, the landlord installs and maintains them.
feedback.wrong: In Toronto, landlords must install smoke alarms and keep them working.

questions.text: A window lock is broken. What do you do?

options.label: Ask the landlord to fix it before move-in, at their cost
Buy and fit a lock yourself
Ignore it

feedback.right: Right: raise it now, before you sign.
feedback.wrong: Ask the landlord to fix locks, at their expense, before move-in.

questions.text: You spot droppings under the sink. What now?

options.label: Raise it with the landlord in writing
Say nothing and buy traps later
Assume it's old and forget it

feedback.right: Right: get it on record before it's your problem.
feedback.wrong: Raise pests with the landlord, in writing, before move-in.

questions.text: Before applying, what's worth asking the landlord?

options.label: What's included: heat, hydro, water, internet, laundry
Who the other tenants are
Nothing, the ad says enough

feedback.wrong: Ask what's included: heat, hydro, water, internet, parking, laundry.

docs.label: Proof of income (job letter or pay stub)
Three months' rent as a deposit

rival.text: Another applicant just offered $100 more a month. Match it?

options.label: Match it: offer $100 more
outcome: Done: your rent is now $100 higher.
That's a budget choice, not a rule.

options.label: Stick with the listed rent
outcome: Your complete application did the talking. You got it!

options.label: Walk away and look at the other offers
outcome: Walking away is always an option.

clauses.plain: Rent is {rent} a month, due on the 1st.
clauses.legal: Tenant shall remit monthly rent of {rent} on or before the first (1st) day of each month.

clauses.plain: A rent deposit of {rent} covers your last month.
clauses.legal: A deposit equal to one (1) month's rent ({rent}) shall be applied to the final month of the tenancy.

clauses.plain: You need tenant liability insurance, and must show proof if asked.
clauses.legal: Tenant shall maintain liability insurance and furnish proof thereof upon Landlord's request.

clauses.plain: This agreement is on Ontario's standard lease form.
clauses.legal: This Residential Tenancy Agreement is made on the Standard Form of Lease prescribed for Ontario.
No animals of any kind shall be kept in or about the Premises.
clauses.why: A term banning pets is void.

clauses.legal: Tenant shall not permit any person to remain in the Premises overnight.
clauses.why: A term banning guests or other occupants is void.

clauses.plain: Plus a $300 damage deposit at signing.
clauses.legal: Tenant shall pay a security deposit of $300 against damage upon execution hereof.
clauses.why: Damage deposits aren't allowed; a rent deposit can't be used as a damage deposit.

clauses.plain: You pay for all repairs, including the furnace and plumbing.
clauses.legal: Tenant assumes responsibility for all repairs to the Premises, including heating and plumbing systems.
clauses.why: A term making you pay for repairs the landlord is responsible for is void.

clauses.plain: The landlord can come in any time, no notice needed.
clauses.legal: Landlord may enter the Premises at any time without prior notice.
clauses.why: Most entries need 24 hours' written notice and an 8 a.m.–8 p.m. time.

question.text: Moving day! Before you unpack, what do you do?

options.label: Photograph every room and any damage, and keep a copy
Unpack first, it can wait
Mention the damage to the landlord in passing
Clean everything first

photos: Smart. Every bit of damage, on record.
unpack: Once your stuff is in, it's hard to prove what was already there.
Photograph every room before you unpack.
verbal: Words are easy to forget or deny.
Photograph the damage, and keep a copy.
clean: Cleaning can hide or blur existing damage.

events.title: January: the heat is out
events.text: January. Your place is freezing, and the heat's been off a day.

actions.label: Message the landlord in writing and keep a copy
Call 311 right away
Stop paying rent until it's fixed

write: Right first step: in writing, and keep a copy.
No heat is urgent: landlords must respond within 24 hours.
311: 311 comes next, if the landlord doesn't fix it.
Start with the landlord, in writing.
withhold: Landlord in writing first, then 311 if unresolved.

events.levelWhy: Toronto's indoor temperature bylaw is a City rule, enforced through 311.

events.title: You spot mice in the kitchen
events.text: You find droppings under the sink. Now there are mice.

actions.label: Send the landlord a written request and keep a copy
Buy traps and say nothing
Call 311 right away

write: Exactly. A written request is your receipt if you need to escalate.
diy: Traps help, but pests are the landlord's job.
Tell them in writing so there's a record.
311: 311 is for when the landlord doesn't act.

events.levelWhy: If the landlord doesn't act, 311 can open a City service request.

events.title: Water drips from the ceiling
events.text: Water drips from the ceiling, through an old stain, right onto your laptop bag.

actions.label: Tell the landlord in writing it's urgent, and keep a copy
Put a bucket under it and wait
Patch it yourself and deduct it from rent

write: Good: urgent, in writing, copy kept.
Still not fixed? 311, or the Landlord and Tenant Board.
wait: A bucket buys time, but leaks get worse.
fix: Deducting repairs from rent isn't an official route.
Ask in writing; escalate via 311 or the Landlord and Tenant Board.

events.levelWhy: The City handles property standards via 311; the Province's tribunal handles maintenance disputes.

photos.with: Your move-in photos show the stain was already there. Clearly the landlord's repair.
photos.without: The landlord says the stain is new and blames you. No photos to prove otherwise.

events.title: No smoke alarm
events.text: You burn toast and notice: no working smoke alarm.

actions.label: Tell the landlord right away, in writing
Ignore it, you'll be careful
Buy one and never mention it

tell: Right. Landlords must install and maintain smoke alarms.
No fix? 311 refers it to Toronto Fire Services.
ignore: Tell the landlord: a working alarm is their job.
buy: A spare is nice, but working alarms are the landlord's job.

events.levelWhy: No fix? 311 refers it to Toronto Fire Services, a City service.

events.title: The window won't lock
events.text: The window lock was broken from day one. Ground floor, too.

actions.label: Ask the landlord in writing to repair it
Tape it shut and hope
Call the police

write: Yes. In writing, with a copy kept for your records.
tape: Ask the landlord in writing to fix it.
police: Police handle crimes and emergencies, not repairs.

events.levelWhy: Repairs not made? The Landlord and Tenant Board (Province) can act.

events.title: A rent increase notice
events.text: A note under your door: "Rent goes up 6% next month."

actions.label: Check the Ontario rules on notice and increases first
Just pay it
Call 311 to complain

check: Smart. Increases generally need 90 days' written notice.
Most units are capped at 2.1% for 2026.
Units first occupied after Nov 15, 2018 are exempt from the cap.
pay: Increases generally need 90 days' written notice; most are capped at 2.1%.
311: Rent increases aren't a City matter.
The rules are provincial; disputes go to the Landlord and Tenant Board.

events.levelWhy: Rent increase rules are provincial; the Landlord and Tenant Board handles disputes.

events.title: Late bus, again
events.text: Your bus was badly late three days this week.

actions.label: Treat it as a City issue: TTC service is a City agency
Complain to your landlord
Nothing anyone can do

city: Right. The TTC is a City agency.
Its service standards set frequency and on-time targets.
landlord: Your landlord can't fix the bus.
TTC service is set through a City agency.
nothing: There is someone: the TTC, a City agency.
Its service standards are under review.

events.levelWhy: The TTC is a City of Toronto agency.

options.label: Text the landlord two weeks before you leave
Give written notice (Form N9) at least 60 days before the end of a rental month
Just move out and leave the keys

text: Too short, and not the right form.
Use Form N9, at least 60 days ahead.
n9: Right: Form N9, at least 60 days ahead.
It ends on the last day of a rental month.
leave: Use Form N9 with at least 60 days' notice.
